title: Does faithful IIT 4.0 big-Phi track transfer entropy (directed flow)? — information-measure arc capstone (Shannon perp / LZ || / TE ||, TE has XOR-synergy blind spot)
question: Across the ECA panel, does faithful state-averaged big-Phi co-vary with total transfer entropy (Pearson r >= 0.5), i.e. does Phi track directed inter-element information FLOW?
engine: HEXAD/IIT4/lib (reused, NOT reinvented): iit4_eca.eca_tpm (next-bit) + iit4_bigphi.big_phi (via stdlib/consciousness/*). Transfer entropy (joint-count) + Pearson/Spearman inlined in the harness.
runtime: $0 mac-local · hexa-only · LLM none · NO GPU · deterministic (cross-process byte-identical)
toolchain_note: built via fix-1180 bypass: HEXA_MAC_BUILD_OK=1 HEXA_LANG=<root> hexa.real.bak-2026-05-22-pre-no-hxc build <src> -o <bin>. See reference-life-cycle-hexa-run-gotchas.

metric_defs.TE_total: sum_{i} sum_{j!=i} TE(j->i), lag-1 bivariate transfer entropy over the uniform 2^n state ensemble. TE(j->i) = sum p(i',i,j) log2[ p(i'|i,j) / p(i'|i) ], i'=next bit of cell i. bits.
metric_defs.Phi_mean: mean over all 2^n states of big_phi(tpm, n, st)[0] (n=4 exact).

seed_hypothesis_H1: Pearson r(TE_total, Phi_mean) >= 0.5 (Phi tracks directed inter-element flow).

rule_150.note: SYNERGY blind-spot: Phi>0 yet bivariate TE=0 (XOR)

information_measure_arc.synthesis: Phi aligns with INTER-ELEMENT flow/complexity (TE, LZ), NOT single-system information (Shannon entropy). Each classical measure has a blind spot: LZ over-predicts on self-similar rule 90 (Phi=0), bivariate TE under-predicts on synergistic XOR rules 150/105 (Phi>0, TE=0). Phi equals none of them exactly and fills both blind spots.

finding: Faithful causal IIT 4.0 big-Phi strongly tracks transfer entropy (directed inter-cell information flow): Pearson r=0.883, Spearman rho=0.822 over the 10-rule panel — the capstone of the information-measure arc. Synthesis with H_287/H_288: Shannon entropy (single-system) is orthogonal to Phi (r=0.363) while the INTER-ELEMENT measures LZ (r=0.831) and TE (r=0.883) align -> Phi is the same axis as inter-element flow/structural complexity, NOT single-system information capacity. HONEST: bivariate TE has an XOR-SYNERGY blind spot — rules 150/105 have Phi=5.625 yet TE_total=0 (XOR integration is synergistic, invisible to pairwise TE conditioning only on i's own present; consistent with the multivariate-information / synergy literature). So each classical measure has a blind spot: LZ over-predicts on self-similar rule 90 (Phi=0), TE under-predicts on synergistic XOR (Phi>0). Phi equals none of them exactly and fills both blind spots — a measurement-fact reason IIT posits Phi as a distinct quantity.
honest_limits: L1 (XOR-SYNERGY blind spot, key): bivariate lag-1 TE gives TE_total=0 for rules 150/105 (XOR) yet Phi=5.625 — synergistic integration is invisible to pairwise TE; r=0.883 is thus an UNDER-estimate, multivariate/causation-entropy TE would recover it. Phi != bivariate TE.
L2: lag-1 bivariate is ONE TE definition; multi-lag, conditional (causation entropy), multivariate TE differ (recover XOR).
L3: Phi_mean averages a state-dependent quantity (FAITHFUL_REMEASURE 4) — direction robust, magnitude state-dependent.
L4: n=4 small, 10-rule panel — r absolute value panel-dependent, direction robust.
L5: ECA rules are flow proxies, not brain/life networks; labels are substrate-themes.
L6: structure-cut big-Phi, not full-IIT4 absolute calibration; correlation robust to scale offset.
L7: verdict is a measurement fact on a toy substrate, NOT 'consciousness = information flow'.

verify_fence.claim: H_290 faithful IIT 4.0 big-Phi TRACKS transfer entropy across a 10-rule ECA panel (Pearson r=0.883, Spearman rho=0.822), completing the arc Shannon-entropy perp Phi (0.363) / LZ-complexity || Phi (0.831) / TE || Phi (0.883) — Phi aligns with inter-element flow/complexity not single-system information; bivariate TE has an XOR-synergy blind spot (rules 150/105: Phi=5.6 yet TE=0); deterministic toy-substrate outcome, NOT an atlas identity
